newsitem.title: ITALY: Farm minister survives no-confidence vote in Italy.
newsitem.headline: Farm minister survives no-confidence vote in Italy.

text.p: Italian Agriculture Minister Michele Pinto survived a no-confidence vote on Tuesday after opposition parties tried to oust him for his handling of a battle with dairy farmers over European Union milk quotas.
The Chamber of Deputies (lower house) voted by 311 to 250 to reject the motion, brought by the hard-right National Alliance party and supported by the separatist Northern League.

Pinto came under fire during a two-week tussle last month between the centre-left government and dairy farmers, who blocked roads and airports to protest against fines levied by the EU for exceeding their production quotas.
The farmers had accused the state of failing to advise them of their correct quotas and initially refused to pay.

The government responded with an offer of cheap loans and payments by instalment and a pledge to set up a commission to examine the farmers' grievances. Italy has also asked the European Commission to increase its milk quota.
